day_shape: 61 items dominated by Khamenei's 'no geographical limits' order to armed forces commanders and SNSC chief Rezaei saying Vance's letter shows US 'tone' has changed, with Rubio saying Trump 'hasn't made a decision' on striking Iran; Qatari mediators held a 12-hour meeting with Tehran, Defa Press claims another tanker struck a mine east of Hormuz, and Iran International reports a 21-year-old protester sentenced to death.

threads.label: Khamenei 'no geographical limits' order
threads.summary: Khamenei's office and IRIB published an order from the Commander-in-Chief to senior military commanders demanding an 'immediate, impactful response without geographical limitation' to any threat, with the target bank to be updated to include all US and Israeli assets. Chief of Staff Ali Abdollahi and the army spokesman echoed the line, and the Jerusalem Post carried the English readout.

threads.label: Vance letter and Qatari mediation track
threads.summary: SNSC Secretary Mohsen Rezaei said on Iranian state TV he had not yet replied to a letter from US Vice President JD Vance but that the American 'tone' had 'completely changed', while Foreign Minister Araghchi called the letter a 'positive step'. The Jerusalem Post reported Qatari mediators held a 12-hour meeting urging Tehran back to talks, and Rubio told reporters at the G20 in Atlanta that Trump 'hasn't made a decision' on striking Iran.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz tanker incident
threads.summary: Defa Press and IRIB reported that another 'illicit' oil tanker caught fire east of the Strait of Hormuz after striking naval mines in what the Iranian Navy described as a prohibited zone. A regime commentator linked European energy strain and French protests to the Hormuz situation, and Defa Press posted on G7's 1 October decision to release up to 100 million barrels over four months.

threads.label: US Treasury pressure campaign and GCC
threads.summary: The US Treasury said its two-month pressure campaign has sharply cut Iran's oil revenue and access to international trade and financial channels, according to Iran International. At a Bahrain summit, the GCC head said Arab states remain open to talks but need a reciprocal response from Tehran, with officials warning of a more destructive phase of the US-Iran war.

threads.label: Yemen and Houthi activity
threads.summary: Defa Press carried Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree's claim of 66 Saudi strikes on Yemen in 24 hours and a total of 3,755 attacks, and reported Houthi political official Mohammad al-Bukhaiti's offer of direct talks with Riyadh under Egyptian mediation. The Jerusalem Post reported Taiz under Houthi siege and said Saudi carrier Riyadh Air had to divert and cancel flights and evacuate aircraft due to Houthi attacks.

threads.label: Domestic repression and legal threats
threads.summary: Iran International reported a court sentenced 21-year-old protester Omran Amani to death for 'moharebeh', and that security forces broke up a Halloween gathering in central Tehran, beating and detaining attendees. The Prosecutor General said Iran will jointly claim war damages from the US, Israel and allied countries.

events.title_en: The EU's dizziness in the energy crisis
events.summary_en: The EU's dizziness in the energy crisis. The decision of the 'Group of Seven' on 1 October to release a maximum of 100 million barrels of crude oil and diesel over four months was taken under US pressure. Donald Trump had previously raised the possibility of stopping US diesel exports; a move that could have exacerbated the supply crisis for this product in Europe. In response, Washington committed not to restrict its energy exports to other members of the Group of Seven. However, just seven days later, Trump reached an agreement with Vladimir Putin on Russian diesel exports to the world market and America; a move that in Europe was seen as a sign of Washington's reluctance to fulfil its commitments to Europe.
